evidence.quote: a quicker pace of easing policy—as I have advocated—would appropriately move us closer to a neutral stance.
Underlying inflation is near, and further approaching, our target.
Yet here we are, keeping interest rates too high because of the phantom inflation of portfolio advisory fees.
Unemployment has trended higher for over two years, and wage growth lower.
Keeping policy unnecessarily tight because of an imbalance from 2022, or because of artifacts of the statistical measurement process, will lead to job losses.
If I am right about shelter but wrong about tariffs, we will undershoot our inflation target.

parsed.rationale: The speaker argues underlying inflation is near target, shelter disinflation will accelerate and tariff effects are noise, while labor market risks are to the downside. He explicitly advocates a quicker pace of easing, a strongly dovish signal.
